title: Ivo and the Current
premise: Riverboat captain Quentin Joubert ferries cargo up the Mekong's tributaries with his adopted crew — engineer Sefa, deckhand twins, and a boy named Ivo he pulled from a flood years ago. When a dying prospector trades a map to a sunken colonial gold cache for a promise of safe passage, Quentin refuses, but the prospector's killers board the boat anyway, forcing the crew to run the river at monsoon's edge. Hunted by a corrupt customs officer who wants the gold buried with his own crimes, they must navigate flooded rapids, a leaking hull, and an uneasy alliance with a riverside village that remembers Quentin's past. In the end, Quentin chooses to sink the treasure rather than let it buy silence, and the village, the crew, and Ivo become the family he stopped running to find.
about_author: Ansel Joubert is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent six years working river routes in Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people whose homes are vessels and whose loyalties are chosen.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A routine cargo run upriver establishes the boat, the crew, and Quentin's rule: never stop moving, never take passengers. Ivo quietly tests that rule by feeding a stowaway child. Emotional beat: warmth under discipline; we see why Quentin keeps distance.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Fare
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At a muddy landing, a feverish prospector named Vann begs passage, offering a hand-drawn map to a sunken French colonial gold cache as payment. Quentin refuses; Ivo, against orders, gives the man water and hears his story. Beat: compassion cracking Quentin's armor.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Vann dies at dawn, but not before Ivo promises to carry the map to his daughter in Luang Prabang. Ivo hides the map from Quentin, guilt and resolve warring. Beat: inheritance begins — a promise made without permission.

chapters.title: Passengers We Didn't Take
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Two men claiming customs authority board at Vientiane, asking pointed questions about Vann. Quentin lies smoothly but recognizes the officer Ravelin from years ago — the man who ruined him. Beat: dread; the past has boarded the boat.

chapters.title: What Ivo Keeps Below
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The engineer discovers Ivo hiding the map in the engine room and covers for him, extracting the truth. Sefa, an exile himself, argues the promise matters more than the risk. Beat: found family deepens through complicity.

chapters.title: Running the Night Water
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin learns of the map and rages — then finds Ravelin's men searching the boat at the next lock. He runs the rapids at night to escape inspection, nearly losing the twins overboard. Beat: commitment; Quentin is now inside the story he refused.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hull
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The escape cracks a seam; the boat takes water faster than the pumps can manage. They beach on a sandbar as the first monsoon storm hits. Beat: vulnerability — the vessel that is their home is failing.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They limp into a riverside village where Quentin once ran supplies during a flood — and where he abandoned people who counted on him. The headwoman, Mai, lets them repair but names the debt aloud. Beat: shame confronted; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Vann's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In Luang Prabang they find Vann's daughter Linh, who reveals the 'gold' is evidence: ledgers proving Ravelin sold confiscated goods and drowned witnesses, sunk with the barge. Beat: the map's true weight — it's not treasure, it's testimony.

chapters.title: Ravelin's Offer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Ravelin corners Quentin privately: give me the map and I'll clear your old conviction, give you back your name and license. Quentin, tempted by legitimacy, asks for one night. Beat: the devil's bargain; inheritance versus identity.

chapters.title: The Twins' Reconnaissance
chapters.summary: Alternating twin POVs, playful and sharp. The twins tail Ravelin's men and learn a gunboat will intercept the Joubert at the gorge in three days. Beat: ticking clock set; the crew becomes a unit with a mission.

chapters.title: Mai's Price
chapters.summary: Mai's POV. The village shelters the boat but Ravelin's men burn a fishing fleet in reprisal. Mai tells Quentin the debt is now blood: help us or leave and be remembered as the man who ran twice. Beat: moral floor; no neutral ground remains.

chapters.title: Storm Season Logic
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa proposes the impossible: run the gorge ahead of the gunboat by riding the monsoon surge, when the rapids are at their deadliest but the patrol can't follow. Quentin must decide whether his skill or his fear rules him. Beat: plan forged from desperation.

chapters.title: What Quentin Buried
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, flashback woven into present. We learn the full story: Quentin once carried Ravelin's contraband unknowingly, took the fall, lost his wife to the disgrace, and has run ever since. Beat: the wound named; stopping costs more because stopping means feeling it.

chapters.title: The Betrayal at the Landing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A crew-adjacent fuel seller sells their position to Ravelin for his brother's freedom. Ivo, sent to buy parts, is captured and the map taken — but he memorized it long ago and gave up a decoy. Beat: loss that isn't loss; Ivo comes of age.

chapters.title: Gorge of the Surge
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The climax run: the Joubert rides the monsoon swell through the gorge while the gunboat grounds itself chasing. The hull nearly folds; the twins lash the cargo; Ivo steers when Quentin is thrown. Beat: terror transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: Raising the Barge
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. With village divers and Linh's knowledge of the site, they raise the sealed ledger chest from the sunken barge as the storm peaks. Beat: the promise kept; inheritance claimed together.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Rather than sell the ledgers or trade them, they copy the evidence and send it to every newspaper, magistrate, and consulate on the river — and give Ravelin's own men copies, dissolving his power from beneath him. Beat: justice as circulation, not transaction.

chapters.title: Ravelin's Last Boarding
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Stripped of backing, Ravelin boards alone with a pistol. Ivo stands between him and Quentin and speaks the truth of what the river does to men who own nothing. Ravelin breaks — arrested by his own subordinates. Beat: the villain undone by the world he corrupted.

chapters.title: The Debt at Mai's Table
chapters.summary: Mai's POV. The village holds a debt-settling feast. Quentin offers the repaired boat's services free each flood season; Mai declares the debt paid and offers Ivo a place among them. Beat: belonging offered and accepted.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin repairs the hull properly, repaints the name, and for the first time moors instead of drifting. He gives Ivo Vann's original map — his inheritance, earned. Beat: stillness chosen, not feared.

chapters.title: The Current Goes On
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing. A year later, the Joubert runs the monsoon route with Linh aboard as navigator and the village as home port. Ivo logs the day's sandbars in the captain's book, learning their moods. Beat: the current continues, but now it carries them home.
